mappings.rationale: LEAD-RULINGS-1520 unblock-types 3: PiG's agent hook takes the call as positional parameters and returns the Pi result type ({}); the context object is the agent loop's own bookkeeping (agent/src/agent-loop.ts builds assistantMessage, toolCall, args, result, isError and context for it) and no Pi code outside the loop reads those members, so no behaviour needs them. A hook signature break is not made here; the members become an additive context argument only if a Pi behaviour reads them.

Reviewed placement onto the positional hook parameters, as the lead ruled on 2026-10-07 (LEAD-RULINGS-1520 unblock-types 3). Pi passes one context object to afterToolCall (agent/src/types.ts:119-132, agent-loop.ts:864-874). Go's AfterToolCallHook (agent/agent.go:658) takes the same values as parameters: toolCall is toolCallID and toolName, args is the validated arguments, and result is the executed result. isError is result.IsError, which finalizeExecutedToolCall (agent/tool_execution.go:456-461) sets to the call's current flag before each hook, as Pi passes isError beside the result. Pi's production hook reads exactly these (agent-session.ts:672-688 _afterToolCall). assistantMessage and context reach every hook through its context.Context as agent.ToolCallHookContext (agent/tool_call_hook_context.go, attached at agent/tool_execution.go:53 and agent/run_tool_call.go:58-59).

mappings.rationale: auth/types.ts:46-48 declares only `signal?: AbortSignal`, an options bag whose single member is the cancellation signal of the auth storage operations read/list/modify/delete (:70-93). Go carries cancellation as the context.Context first parameter of every such operation (AGENTS.md: AbortSignal and request/session lifetime map to context.Context), so the bag has no Go counterpart: ModelsStore.Read/Write/Delete and the Auth storage methods take ctx. Designed out by the lead's ruling of 2026-10-07 15:20 MDT (language mechanics with no Go meaning are designed out with a citation).

types.ts:490 JsonRepresentation<T> is a conditional type (IsAny/unknown/extends JsonValue) that computes the JSON-serialised type of T at compile time; it has no runtime value. Go values cross JSON through encoding/json with a concrete Go type, so there is no type to compute. Its only consumer, ToolResultMessage.details (types.ts:602), is ai.ToolResultMessage.Details. Designed out by the lead's ruling of 2026-10-07 15:20 MDT (language mechanics with no Go meaning are designed out with a citation).

ai types.ts:454 `JsonValue` is the closed union of JSON value kinds (null, boolean, number, string, array, object) that TypeScript needs to type parsed JSON. Go decodes JSON into `any` (encoding/json: nil, bool, float64, string, []any, map[string]any), which is the same value space; the typed forms live where Pi types them (ai.ToolSchema, ai.ToolCall arguments, JsonRepresentation => any in representations.json). Designed out: the union has no Go declaration to port.

types.ts:490 JsonRepresentation<T> is a conditional type (IsAny/unknown/extends JsonValue) that computes the JSON-serialised type of T at compile time; it has no runtime value. Go values cross JSON through encoding/json with a concrete Go type, so there is no type to compute. Its only consumer, ToolResultMessage.details (types.ts:602), is ai.ToolResultMessage.Details. Designed out by the lead's ruling of 2026-10-07 15:20 MDT (language mechanics with no Go meaning are designed out with a citation).

ai types.ts:454 `JsonValue` is the closed union of JSON value kinds (null, boolean, number, string, array, object) that TypeScript needs to type parsed JSON. Go decodes JSON into `any` (encoding/json: nil, bool, float64, string, []any, map[string]any), which is the same value space; the typed forms live where Pi types them (ai.ToolSchema, ai.ToolCall arguments, JsonRepresentation => any in representations.json). Designed out: the union has no Go declaration to port.

TG: AnyTask (harness/types.ts:91) is the object type `{ readonly definition: {...erased task definition...}; ... }` that a task satisfies structurally. A Go interface cannot declare a field, and Go's Task[I,S,R,H] already has a field Definition (the typed *TaskDefinition), so the erased definition is read through the interface method AnyDefinition() *AnyTaskDefinition (name, version, initial, phases, abort, migrate, hooks, all carried by AnyTaskDefinition). Designed out as language mechanics with no Go meaning (a field-bearing object type becomes an accessor on a consumer-owned interface), as LEAD-RULINGS-1520 (2026-10-07) rules for this class. The registry takes AnyTask and every Task satisfies it.

mappings.rationale: TG: the callback type AddClientAuthentication (oauth/flow.ts:34-39) declares `url: string | URL`, and the only caller, the token request (flow.ts:210), passes its URL value. TypeScript writes the union so a handler may name either spelling; Go has one URL type, so mcp/oauth.AddClientAuthentication takes the *url.URL the flow passes (flow.go:71), and a handler that wants the string calls url.String(). The string spelling carries no input a Go handler can be given that the URL does not. Designed out as language mechanics with no Go meaning (a string-or-URL union over one Go URL type), as LEAD-RULINGS-1520 (2026-10-07) rules for this class.

Pi's `_schemas` parameter is typed `Schemas & UniqueTelemetrySchemas<Schemas>` (telemetry/src/index.ts:349-352). UniqueTelemetrySchemas is a compile-time brand: when two schemas of the tuple declare the same span name it adds the member `readonly "duplicate telemetry span names"`, so the call fails to type-check (index.ts:279-298). The member is never a run-time value, and the function ignores its schemas at run time (bindTypedSpanStarter(telemetryContext), index.ts:352-355; 'no runtime schema validation is performed'). StdinBuffer extends Node's EventEmitter (packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts), so these are inherited EventEmitter members with no Go form. Designed out as JavaScript EventEmitter mechanics, as LEAD-RULINGS-1520 allows for language mechanics with no Go meaning (the rule request is in docs/parity/gap-closure/ledger-help-8-tui-rule-requests.md).

PiG renders Markdown with its own Go parser in tui/markdown*.go and exposes no marked-shaped parser or token types, so there is no Go declaration to port. Designed out as a third-party re-export, as the ai typebox re-exports (Static, TSchema, Type) are.
